It sounds really exhausting to feel stuck in that loop of repetitive thoughts. What you're describing is common, and there are a few things that might help. Try gently redirecting your attention to something engaging but not demanding—like a walk, a simple task, or describing your surroundings in detail. Some people find it helpful to set a timer and allow themselves 10 minutes to write down everything they're thinking, then close the notebook and shift activities. Grounding exercises, like focusing on your breath or noticing five things you can see, can also interrupt the cycle.

It's okay if the thoughts come back—try not to judge yourself for that. Each time you notice them returning, you can practice gently shifting your focus again. If this pattern is persistent, distressing, or interfering with your daily life, consider reaching out to a mental health professional who can help you explore what's underneath it and develop strategies tailored to you. You don't have to figure this out alone.
